_comment: System tests and bug reports (FACTORY.md §4b, §4c). Copy to .github/factory-testing.json to turn them on for this repo. With system_tests true, the Test Planner runs between the Planner and the Architect, writes system-tests/test-plan.md and system-tests/test-data.md into the epic's change folder, and opens one test(<epic>) sub-issue per case; the Dispatcher releases each case to factory:manual-test once the code it depends on is assembled, and a human comments exactly 'Test Passed' or 'Test Failed' on it. An absent or unparseable file means system_tests false: no Test Planner, no test sub-issues, and every other behaviour exactly as before. mode 'gate' (the default when the file is present) holds an epic short of factory:epic-ready until every open case has passed and no bug is open; 'advisory' flips the epic as it does today and lists the open cases and bugs as unverified. mode has no effect on a repo with no epic branch (epics false): there the code first reaches a shared branch at gate GS, so the cases run on staging and their verdicts are evidence in the promotion PR, never a hold — gate G3 is a human's merge click. run_on says where a human runs the cases: 'epic' (the default when absent) releases each case as the tasks it depends on are assembled onto the epic branch, to be run on the epic's preview environment; 'staging' lets the epic reach factory:epic-ready on assembly alone, gate GS puts it on staging, and the Dispatcher releases each case once the tasks it depends on are factory:in-staging — cases and bugs then never hold GS, their verdicts are evidence at G3, and mode has no effect (the same posture as epics false). A staging approver (falling back to the release list) can comment exactly 'Skip tests' on an epic from factory:design-approved onward to close every open case as factory:test-skipped without running it, or on one test(<epic>) case to skip that case alone; bug reports are never skipped. An epic already past G2 when this file lands has no plan; comment 'Plan tests' on it to write one. bug_reports lets a tester raise what no case predicted: commenting 'Bug' on an epic (with the report underneath), or filing an issue labelled factory:bug, opens a bug(<epic>) sub-issue and files an ordinary task to fix it onto the epic branch (§4c). Absent, it follows system_tests; set it false to keep the cases without the bugs, or set it true with system_tests false for exploratory testing with no written plan.
